messages.author: e388c645dd8088ba
messages.subject: DIC and AIC are equal?
parts:
Hi Phil,

Thank you for all the work you put into the mirt package: it's a life-saver! 

I have been working on my dissertation comparing several different IRT models for an instrument.  All of the models converged successfully and without any warnings.  However, when I examine the AIC and DIC values for every model, the values are identical.  My (limited) understanding of these fit measures is that it is very unlikely that they are identical, especially in multiple models. 

Below I have pasted the output from calling the object as well as the DIC values, with the AIC and DIC values highlighted.  The same problem occurs when I ran the models as generalized partial credit models as well.  Any light you could shine on this oddity would be greatly appreciated. 

Thanks,
Dave Periard
Ph.D Candidate in Industrial/Organizational Psychology and Human Factors
Wright State University

###Unidimensional Graded Response Model
> MBI_UNI_RUN

Call:
mirt(data = MBI_FS, model = MBI_UNI, itemtype = "graded", SE = T, 
    SE.type = "crossprod", method = "MHRM")

Full-information item factor analysis with 1 factor(s).
Converged within 0.001 tolerance after 36 MHRM iterations.
mirt version: 1.16 
M-step optimizer: NR 

Information matrix estimated with method: MHRM
Condition number of information matrix = 700.9893
Second-order test: model is a possible local maximum

Log-likelihood = -205234.4, SE = 0.12
AIC = 410776.7; AICc = 410783.2
BIC = 411842.4; SABIC = 411353.1
> MBI_UNI_RUN@Fit$DIC
[1] 410776.7
> 
> ###Correlated Traits Graded Response Model
> MBI_CT_RUN

Call:
mirt(data = MBI_FS, model = MBI_CT, itemtype = "graded", SE = T, 
    SE.type = "crossprod", method = "MHRM")

Full-information item factor analysis with 3 factor(s).
Converged within 0.001 tolerance after 65 MHRM iterations.
mirt version: 1.16 
M-step optimizer: NR 

Information matrix estimated with method: MHRM
Condition number of information matrix = 3152.361
Second-order test: model is not a maximum, or the information matrix is too inaccurate

Log-likelihood = -198960.3, SE = 0.116
AIC = 398234.5; AICc = 398241.3
BIC = 399321; SABIC = 398822.1
> MBI_CT_RUN@Fit$DIC
[1] 398234.5
> 
> ###Bifactor Graded Response Model
> MBI_BF_RUN

Call:
bfactor(data = MBI_FS, model = MBI_BF, SE = T, SE.type = "crossprod", 
    itemtype = "graded", technical = list(NCYCLES = 5000))

Full-information item factor analysis with 4 factor(s).
Converged within 1e-04 tolerance after 1020 EM iterations.
mirt version: 1.16 
M-step optimizer: BFGS 
EM acceleration: Ramsay
Number of rectangular quadrature: 31

Information matrix estimated with method: crossprod
Condition number of information matrix = 2309.428
Second-order test: model is a possible local maximum

Log-likelihood = -196906.7
AIC = 394165.5; AICc = 394174
BIC = 395383.4; SABIC = 394824.1
> MBI_BF_RUN@Fit$DIC
[1] 394165.5

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: DIC and AIC are equal?
parts:
AIC and DIC will be identical when no prior parameter distributions are included. So this is the correct result. I would probably just report AIC though because these models don't have priors. Cheers.

Phil
